text.tspan: CloudFront vs Global Accelerator: same edge network, different jobs
Both: use the AWS global network and its edge locations around the world · both integrate with AWS Shield for DDoS protection
Both: help global users get low latency to an app in one or more AWS Regions
CDN: caches content at the edge
network-layer proxy: packets go over AWS backbone
YES: content served FROM the edge
NO caching: every request reaches your app
S3, VPC origins, ALB, NLB, EC2, any HTTP
ALB, NLB, EC2, Elastic IP (can be internal)
WAF, geo restriction, OAC, signed URLs, invalid.
traffic dials, endpoint weights, client affinity
per GB out + per request (or flat-rate plan)
fixed hourly fee + Data Transfer-Premium per GB
• "static IP", "allowlist IPs", "UDP", "gaming", "IoT/MQTT", "VoIP", "fast Regional failover without DNS" → Global Accelerator.
• HTTP app that needs fixed IPs or deterministic failover → Global Accelerator (even though it is HTTP).
